objective: Give the isolated OpenClaw Engineering Lead a durable one-worker task queue with dependency gates, revision-fenced checkpoints, bounded retries, native task-ledger reconciliation, and same-lane restart recovery.
acceptanceCriteria: Each exact manifest is enqueued once in a managed OpenClaw Task Flow whose state survives gateway restart and rejects stale revision writes.
The oldest eligible task is claimed only after every declared dependency has a succeeded supervision flow, and no second worker can be dispatched while one is ready or running.

A dispatch binds one attempt, deterministic dispatch key, stable OpenClaw task name and label, exact lane prompt, pinned worker timeout and native task-run identity without incrementing on repeated recovery.
Native succeeded, failed, timed-out, cancelled and lost task states reconcile deterministically; only retryable outcomes resume the same manifest lane and retries cannot exceed the manifest limit.
A succeeded worker must provide a strict completion report that matches the manifest, branch, base, attempt, cost and live lane evidence before the flow succeeds.
A gateway-restart recovery pass returns the existing dispatch, waits on an active native run, or creates one bounded same-lane retry without duplicating a branch, worktree, attempt or task flow.
The Engineering Lead has only the narrow supervision and lane tools; worker, reviewer, merge and production boundaries remain unchanged.
stopConditions: A manifest, dependency, flow owner, revision, lane, native task, worker identity or completion identity does not match exactly.
A retry would exceed the manifest attempt, time or cost limit or would follow a blocked, unsafe, cancelled or unclassified outcome.
Recovery would create a second active worker, branch, worktree, flow or attempt instead of resuming the existing owner evidence.
Implementation would enable merge, deployment, production access, customer contact, raw credentials, general supervisor shell access or an unrelated scheduler.
